# menus


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A host describes its menu bar as data: a list of menus, each with a
title and a list of rows. This module defines the row types, and the
small part of a keymap a menu needs to read. They are plain dataclasses
that do not import pywebview or AppKit, so a host can build and test its
menu table on any machine. `kavacha.window` turns the table into a
native menu bar on macOS.

### The rows

[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
is a row that runs one of the host’s actions, named by `action`. When
the user chooses it, the window calls the host’s `on_action` with that
name. A
[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
with no action is a separator line, which is why `action` has a default.
`kind` is either empty or `warn`. `warn` marks a row the host may want
to draw as destructive, such as one that discards changes; kavacha
passes it through without acting on it, and refuses any other value.

### MenuItem

``` python
def MenuItem(
    action:str='', kind:str=''
)->None:
```

*One action in a menu. A blank action is a separator.*

``` python
MenuItem('open_folder'), MenuItem()
```

[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) is a row
that AppKit already knows how to handle, such as Cut, Copy, Paste and
Select All, so the host does not handle it at all. The row names an
AppKit selector, such as `cut:`. The menu sends that selector along
AppKit’s responder chain, the chain of objects that starts at whatever
has keyboard focus, and the first one that understands it acts. `key`
and `mods` give the row’s shortcut directly, because a row like this has
no entry in the host’s keymap.

[`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js) is a row
that runs a JavaScript expression in the focused window, for small jobs
such as reloading the page that need no action of their own.

### Key bindings

A menu shows each action’s label and shortcut, and the host keeps both
in its keymap. kavacha does not read the keymap itself. The host
supplies a lookup function that takes an action name and returns a
[`Binding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding),
or `None` for an action it does not know. A
[`Binding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding)
holds the action’s chords, its label, and its scope, meaning where the
binding applies. A `global` binding becomes a menu shortcut. A binding
with another scope becomes one only when `shared` is false, which the
host sets when no other scope binds the same chord. A dict’s `get`
method is the simplest lookup, as in the example.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/kavacha/blob/main/kavacha/menus.py#L39"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Binding

``` python
def Binding(
    keys:tuple=(), label:str='', scope:str='global', shared:bool=False
)->None:
```

*What a menu row reads from the host’s keymap: the chords, the label,
where it applies, and whether another scope binds its chord.*

``` python
keys = {'save': Binding(('mod+s',), 'Save'), 'find': Binding(('mod+f',), scope='editor')}
keys.get('save'), keys.get('nothing')
```

`bound` is true when the binding has at least one chord. It is worked
out from `keys` instead of being stored, so an unbound action is just
[`Binding()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding)
and the two can never disagree.

### Chords a menu must not take

A menu shortcut wins over the web page, so a chord the system or a
window manager already uses must never become one. `RESERVED` lists them
in the keymap grammar: Hyper (`hyper`, Command, Control, Option and
Shift together) with the keys AeroSpace takes, AeroSpace’s own Control
and Option chords, and the macOS system chords.
[`kavacha.window.menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
refuses every one of them, and a host can lint its default keymap
against the same set.

The launcher’s own rows are
[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) rows every
Mac app has. `LAUNCHER_ROWS` lists them with their chords, so a host can
check that no chord on its own menu bar lands on one of them. Close
Window takes ⇧⌘W, which leaves ⌘W for the host’s Close Tab.

### How a chord is written for a person

[`chord_glyph`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#chord_glyph)
writes one chord the way a Mac menu does: the modifier glyphs in the
order ⌃⌥⇧⌘, then the key as a capital letter or a symbol such as ↩ or ⌫.
With `mac=False` it writes `Ctrl+Shift+P`. `mod` is Command on a Mac and
Control elsewhere, `hyper` is all four modifiers, and a capital letter
means Shift. A sequence of chords separated by spaces keeps its spaces.
Every place a host shows a chord, such as its menus, palette, help and
toasts, can use this one function, so they all agree.

chord_glyph('mod+shift+p'), chord_glyph('alt+shift+b'), chord_glyph('mod+enter'), chord_glyph('mod+shift+p', mac=False)
```

### Keys off a Mac

On Linux and Windows, `mod` is Control. Most chords keep their meaning,
but some do not. ⌃⌘F, the Mac chord for Full Screen, becomes Ctrl+F,
which is Find. Hide and Minimize have no use under a tiling window
manager such as Regolith’s i3 or sway.
[`pc_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#pc_key)
gives the chord a
[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) row takes
off a Mac. A Mac-only row takes the chord from a small table: Full
Screen is F11, Close Window is Ctrl+Shift+W and Quit is Ctrl+Q. Hide,
Hide Others, Minimize, Zoom and Bring All to Front get `None`, which
means that the row is not shown. Every other row keeps its chord, with
`mod` as Control.
[`pc_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#pc_chord)
writes any chord in this PC form.

`LINUX_RESERVED` lists the chords a Linux desktop keeps for itself:
Regolith’s and GNOME’s.
[`pc_reserved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#pc_reserved)
also refuses every chord with Super, because Regolith owns almost all of
them. A host can lint its PC keymap against the same set.

[`gtk_accel`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#gtk_accel)
writes a chord as a GTK accelerator, such as `<Control><Shift>w`. GTK
runs a window’s accelerators before the widget that has focus. A native
accelerator on Copy would take Ctrl+C away from a terminal in the page,
so
[`menu_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_json)
gives one only to rows the page never needs. `PC_NATIVE` names those
launcher rows: Quit, Close Window and Full Screen.

    chord

```

*One chord off a Mac, as `ctrl+alt+shift+super+base` with `mod` folded

``` python
{r.title: pc_key(r) for r in LAUNCHER_ROWS}
```

    {'Quit': 'ctrl+q',
     'Hide': None,
     'Hide Others': None,
     'Close Window': 'ctrl+shift+w',
     'Undo': 'ctrl+z',
     'Redo': 'ctrl+shift+z',
     'Minimize': None,
     'Enter Full Screen': 'f11'}

[`kavacha.window.menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
takes the menu table and the lookup function together. kavacha ships no
default table for either, because what belongs on an app’s File menu is
up to the app.
